title: Interactive Caption Editor (Opus Clip-like Experience)

overview.problem: The studio editor currently runs on mock/hardcoded data with no real video playback, no real transcript data, and no caption editing. Captions are only burned into the video during FFmpeg rendering in the worker — users cannot preview or edit captions before rendering. This means every text correction requires a full re-render, wasting time and credits.
overview.solution: Build an Opus Clip-like interactive caption editor where source video plays in the browser with captions overlaid as HTML/CSS elements, synced word-by-word to playback. Users can edit transcript text, customize caption styling, and preview everything in real-time before triggering a final render.
overview.reference_product: clip.opus.pro/editor-ux/ — left transcript panel, center video preview with HTML caption overlay, right tool sidebar with caption styling, bottom timeline
success_criteria: User can open the studio for any clip and see the source video playing with captions overlaid
Captions highlight the active word in real-time as the video plays
User can edit any transcript text and see the caption overlay update instantly
User can change caption styling (font, color, position, outline, shadow, highlight color) and see it preview on the video immediately
Edits are auto-saved and persist across page reloads
Final render uses the edited transcript and caption preset

personas.name: Content Creator
personas.description: A YouTuber or social media creator who uploads long-form videos and uses Narriflow to automatically detect viral-worthy clips. They want to fine-tune the auto-generated captions before exporting clips to TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.
goals: Quickly fix transcription errors (names, jargon, filler words)
Customize caption look to match their brand
Preview the final result before spending credits on a render
Export clips in multiple aspect ratios with consistent styling
pain_points: Cannot see what captions will look like without rendering
Every text fix requires a full re-render
No way to edit transcript text in the current UI
Mock data in editor doesn't reflect actual clip content

phases.name: Word-Level Timing in Data Layer
phases.description: Capture per-word timing from Deepgram transcription so captions can highlight individual words during playback.

phases.name: Extend Caption Preset Schema
phases.description: Add missing fields (highlightColor, animation, center position) to the captionPreset DB schema so they persist and are available to the worker.

phases.name: Real Video Playback & Server Data Loading
phases.description: Replace mock data with real clip data and stream the source video in the browser. This is the highest-impact change — the studio goes from mock demo to real editor.

phases.name: Real-Time Word-Synced Caption Overlay
phases.description: Replace hardcoded mock captions with real word-by-word highlighting synced to video playback.

phases.name: Editable Transcript Panel
phases.description: Make transcript text editable in the left panel with auto-save, so users can fix transcription errors and the overlay updates in real-time.

phases.name: Worker Rendering with Word-Level Captions
phases.description: Update FFmpeg rendering to use word-level timing for rapid caption cues (2-3 words at a time) instead of full utterances.

user_stories.title: View real video with caption overlay
user_stories.i_want: to open the studio editor for a clip and see the actual source video playing with captions overlaid on top
user_stories.so_that: I can preview exactly how the clip will look before rendering
acceptance_criteria: When I navigate to /projects/{id}/clips/{clipId}/studio, the actual source video loads and displays in the center panel
The placeholder gradient disappears once the video loads
The video starts at the clip's startSec position in the source, not at 0:00
Play/pause controls (spacebar, play button) work with the real video
The timeline playhead and current time display update as the video plays
The video stops playing when it reaches the clip's endSec boundary
Seeking via timeline click, arrow keys, and keyboard shortcuts works correctly
If no source video exists (e.g., audio-only), the placeholder gradient remains visible

technical_notes.video_source: Presigned R2 URL with 1-hour TTL, generated in server component via presignDownloadUrl()
technical_notes.time_system: All UI uses clip-relative time (0 to duration). Video element uses absolute project time. Translation: clipRelative = video.currentTime - clipStartSec
technical_notes.fallback: If sourceVideoUrl is null, keep the existing simulated playback timer for demo mode

user_stories.title: See word-by-word caption highlighting
user_stories.i_want: to see captions appear word-by-word over the video, with the currently spoken word highlighted in a different color
user_stories.so_that: I can verify the caption timing and visual effect match my expectations before rendering
acceptance_criteria: As the video plays, a 2-3 word caption window appears over the video, advancing as speech progresses
The currently active word (being spoken) is highlighted in the highlightColor (default: #00ff88)
Non-active words display in the primaryColor (default: #FFFFFF)
The caption position matches the preset: top (10% from top), center (vertically centered), or bottom (12% from bottom)
The caption font matches the preset fontName (e.g., 'Bebas Neue')
The caption has the correct outline (text-stroke) and shadow effects from the preset
When the video is paused, the caption for the current position remains visible
When no speech is happening (between utterances), no caption is shown
Clips without word-level timing gracefully fall back to showing the full utterance text without per-word highlighting

technical_notes.hook: useCurrentCaption(currentTime, utterances, clipStartSec) returns { visibleWords, activeWordIndex }
technical_notes.window_size: 3 words (configurable), centered on the active word
technical_notes.animation: word-by-word sliding window only for initial implementation
technical_notes.css_outline: Generated from outlineWidth + outlineColor via multi-directional text-shadow

user_stories.title: Customize caption styling with live preview
user_stories.i_want: to change caption font, colors, position, outline, and shadow in the Captions panel and see the changes instantly on the video preview
user_stories.so_that: I can fine-tune the visual style of my captions to match my brand without re-rendering
acceptance_criteria: Opening the Captions tool panel shows the existing caption style controls
Changing the font immediately updates the caption overlay on the video
Changing the text color (primaryColor) immediately updates non-active words on the overlay
Changing the highlight color immediately updates the active word on the overlay
Changing the position (top/center/bottom) immediately repositions the caption overlay
Changing outline width/color immediately updates the text stroke effect
Toggling bold on/off immediately changes the font weight on the overlay
Toggling shadow on/off immediately changes the drop shadow effect
The preview box in the Captions panel also reflects the current styling
Style changes are auto-saved after 1500ms of inactivity

technical_notes.state_flow: CaptionsPanel updates captionPreset in StudioShell context → CaptionOverlay reads from context and re-renders
technical_notes.already_works: The CaptionsPanel already updates captionPreset in context. The main work is ensuring the new CaptionOverlay reads ALL preset fields correctly.

user_stories.title: Edit transcript text
user_stories.i_want: to click on any transcript segment in the left panel and edit the text directly
user_stories.so_that: I can fix transcription errors, remove filler words, and customize what the captions say
acceptance_criteria: Each speech block in the transcript panel is clickable and becomes editable on focus
When I type, the text updates in place (contentEditable behavior)
When I blur the field (click away), the caption overlay immediately shows the updated text
Word timing is automatically recalculated using proportional redistribution when text changes
The utterance shows a visual indicator (e.g., subtle highlight) when it has been modified
I can undo text changes with Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z
Empty text (all content deleted) is rejected — the original text remains
The edited text is used in the caption overlay, not the original transcription text

technical_notes.editing_approach: contentEditable div per utterance, not textarea
technical_notes.timing_recalc: When text changes from N words to M words, redistribute the utterance's [startSec, endSec] duration equally among M words
technical_notes.state: utterances stored as mutable useState in StudioShell context, updateUtteranceText(index, newText) function

user_stories.title: Click word to seek to timestamp
user_stories.i_want: to click on any word in the transcript panel to jump the video to that exact moment
user_stories.so_that: I can quickly navigate to specific parts of the clip for review
acceptance_criteria: When I click a word in the transcript (when not in editing mode), the video seeks to that word's startSec
The timeline playhead jumps to the corresponding position
The caption overlay updates to show the words around the clicked word
The active word in the caption highlights the clicked word
If I click a word while the video is paused, it seeks but stays paused
If I click a word while the video is playing, it seeks and continues playing

technical_notes.implementation: Each word rendered as a <span> with onClick handler calling seekTo(word.startSec - clipStartSec)
technical_notes.mode_switching: Click-to-seek only works when NOT in editing mode (isEditing === false). When focused for editing, clicks go to normal text cursor positioning

user_stories.title: Auto-save edits
user_stories.i_want: my transcript and caption style changes to be saved automatically
user_stories.so_that: I don't lose my work if I navigate away or close the browser
acceptance_criteria: After I stop making changes for 1500ms, the editor auto-saves both captionPreset and transcriptSlice
The save indicator in the top bar shows: 'Save changes' (idle) → 'Saving...' (in progress) → 'Saved ✓' (complete)
The 'Saved ✓' indicator returns to 'Save changes' after 2 seconds
If I click the Save button manually, it saves immediately without waiting for the debounce
After saving, reloading the page shows the previously saved changes
If the save fails (network error), the save state returns to idle (not 'Saved')
The first render after page load does NOT trigger a save (only user-initiated changes)

technical_notes.api_calls: Two sequential PATCH requests to /api/projects/{id}/clips/{clipId}: one with { captionPreset }, one with { transcriptSlice }
technical_notes.initial_render_guard: useRef(isInitialRender) set to true, flipped to false after first effect run

user_stories.title: Active utterance auto-scroll in transcript
user_stories.i_want: the transcript panel to automatically scroll to the currently playing utterance
user_stories.so_that: I can follow along with the speech as the video plays without manually scrolling
acceptance_criteria: As the video plays, the active utterance (containing the current playback time) is highlighted with a subtle background color
The transcript panel automatically scrolls to keep the active utterance visible
If I manually scroll the transcript, auto-scroll pauses for 3 seconds to avoid fighting with the user
After 3 seconds of no manual scrolling, auto-scroll resumes
The active utterance highlighting updates smoothly without flicker

technical_notes.active_detection: absoluteTime = currentTime + clipStartSec; utterance is active when absoluteTime >= u.startSec && absoluteTime < u.endSec
technical_notes.manual_scroll_pause: Set a timestamp on scroll event, skip auto-scroll if < 3 seconds since last manual scroll

user_stories.title: Render uses edited transcript and captions
user_stories.i_want: the final rendered video to use my edited transcript text and caption styling, with rapid word-by-word caption cues
user_stories.so_that: the exported clip matches what I previewed in the editor
acceptance_criteria: When I trigger a render after editing the transcript, the rendered video shows the edited text, not the original
The rendered video shows rapid 2-3 word caption cues instead of full utterance blocks
Caption styling (font, color, outline, shadow, position) in the render matches the saved captionPreset
If I set position to 'center', the captions appear vertically centered in the render
If an utterance has no word-level timing (fallback), the render uses a single utterance-level cue (original behavior)
The render completes without errors for all aspect ratios (9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:5)

technical_notes.srt_generation: generateSrtFromSlice() now groups words into 2-3 word cues when words[] is available
technical_notes.center_alignment: ASS Alignment=5 for center position (vs 8 for top, 2 for bottom)
technical_notes.highlight_limitation: highlightColor is NOT applied in rendered output (preview-only). Render uses uniform primaryColor. This matches Opus Clip behavior.

user_stories.title: Word-level timing captured from Deepgram
user_stories.i_want: the transcription pipeline to capture per-word timing (start, end, word, confidence) from Deepgram responses
user_stories.so_that: the studio editor can display word-by-word caption highlighting
acceptance_criteria: After transcription, each TranscriptUtterance has an optional words[] array
Each word object has: word (string), startSec (number), endSec (number), confidence (number|null)
The words use punctuated_word from Deepgram (includes capitalization and punctuation) when available, falling back to plain word
Words without valid start/end timestamps are filtered out
Existing utterances without words[] are still valid (field is optional)
The TranscriptWord Zod schema validates word objects correctly

technical_notes.deepgram_api: Deepgram Nova-3 with utterances=true already returns words[] per utterance with start, end, word, punctuated_word, confidence
technical_notes.current_gap: normalizeDeepgramTranscript() currently discards word data — only keeps utterance-level text and timing
technical_notes.backward_compat: words field is z.array(transcriptWordSchema).optional() — existing data without words passes validation

user_stories.title: Extended caption preset with highlight and animation
user_stories.i_want: the captionPreset schema to support highlightColor, animation mode, and center position
user_stories.so_that: these settings persist in the database and are available to both the editor UI and the worker
acceptance_criteria: captionPresetSchema now accepts position: 'center' in addition to 'top' and 'bottom'
captionPresetSchema now accepts highlightColor as an optional hex color string
captionPresetSchema now accepts animation as an optional enum: 'none', 'word-by-word', 'karaoke', 'bounce'
Existing captionPreset values in the database (without new fields) still parse correctly
The worker maps center position to ASS Alignment=5

technical_notes.all_fields_optional: New fields are optional, maintaining backward compatibility
technical_notes.worker_support: Only 'center' position is applied in the worker initially. highlightColor and animation are preview-only.

user_journeys.title: First-time studio editing experience
user_journeys.description: A user opens the studio editor for a clip for the first time and previews captions on the real video.

steps.action: User navigates to /projects/{projectId}/clips/{clipId}/studio
steps.system_behavior: Server component loads: authenticates user, fetches clip data (with transcriptSlice containing word-level timing), fetches project data, generates presigned URL for source video. Passes all data as props to StudioShell client component.
steps.user_sees: The studio editor loads with: top bar (title, save, export), left transcript panel, center video preview (loading), right tool sidebar, bottom timeline.

steps.action: Video loads automatically
steps.system_behavior: VideoPreview component sets video.src to presigned URL. On loadedmetadata, seeks to clipStartSec. setVideoLoaded(true) hides placeholder gradient and shows <video> element.
steps.user_sees: The placeholder gradient fades away and the actual source video appears, showing the first frame of the clip. Captions appear at the bottom (default position).

steps.action: User presses spacebar to play
steps.system_behavior: togglePlay() calls video.play(). setIsPlaying(true). timeupdate events fire, updating currentTime. useCurrentCaption hook finds active utterance and word based on currentTime + clipStartSec.
steps.user_sees: Video starts playing. Captions show a 3-word window that slides forward as speech progresses. The currently spoken word is highlighted in green (#00ff88). Timeline playhead moves. Transcript panel scrolls and highlights the active utterance.

steps.action: User pauses to review a specific caption
steps.system_behavior: togglePlay() calls video.pause(). setIsPlaying(false). currentTime stops updating.
steps.user_sees: Video pauses. The caption overlay shows the word group at the current position. The active word remains highlighted.

steps.action: User clicks the Captions tool in the right sidebar
steps.system_behavior: setActiveTool('captions'). CaptionsPanel slides in from the right.
steps.user_sees: The captions styling panel opens with: font selector, style toggles (bold/shadow/outline), color pickers (text/highlight/outline), outline width slider, position toggles (top/center/bottom), preview box showing current style.

steps.action: User changes the font to 'Impact' and highlight color to yellow (#FFD700)
steps.system_behavior: setCaptionPreset updates fontName and highlightColor in context. CaptionOverlay re-renders with new font and highlight color.
steps.user_sees: The caption overlay on the video immediately switches to Impact font and the active word turns yellow. The preview box in the panel also updates.

steps.action: User resumes playback to see the new style
steps.system_behavior: togglePlay(). Video plays. Captions continue with updated styling.
steps.user_sees: Video plays with Impact font captions and yellow word highlighting. Looks great!

steps.action: User waits 1.5 seconds without making changes
steps.system_behavior: Auto-save debounce timer fires. PATCH /api/projects/{id}/clips/{clipId} with { captionPreset }. setSaveState('saving') → 'saved' → 'idle'.
steps.user_sees: Top bar save indicator briefly shows 'Saving...' then 'Saved ✓'.

user_journeys.title: Editing transcript to fix transcription errors
user_journeys.description: A user notices a transcription error and corrects it in the transcript panel.

steps.action: User is playing the clip and hears 'SHERP' but sees 'SHIRT' in the transcript
steps.system_behavior: Transcript panel shows the active utterance with 'SHIRT' text. Caption overlay shows 'SHIRT'.
steps.user_sees: The word 'SHIRT' is wrong — it should be 'SHERP' (the vehicle name).

steps.action: User clicks on the utterance containing 'SHIRT'
steps.system_behavior: The utterance block gets focus, entering editing mode (isEditing = true). contentEditable is activated.
steps.user_sees: The utterance text gets a subtle blue border/background indicating it's editable. A text cursor appears.

steps.action: User selects 'SHIRT' and types 'SHERP'
steps.system_behavior: Standard contentEditable text editing. The DOM text updates.
steps.user_sees: The text changes from 'SHIRT' to 'SHERP' in the transcript panel.

steps.action: User clicks away from the utterance (blur event)
steps.system_behavior: handleBlur fires. Detects text changed. Calls updateUtteranceText(index, newText). This: (1) updates utterance.text, (2) recalculates word timing via proportional redistribution, (3) triggers auto-save debounce.
steps.user_sees: The caption overlay now shows 'SHERP' instead of 'SHIRT'. The transcript text is updated. Save indicator shows 'Saving...' after 1.5s.

steps.action: User plays the clip again to verify
steps.system_behavior: Video plays. useCurrentCaption uses the updated utterance with new word timing.
steps.user_sees: The caption at that moment now correctly shows 'SHERP' with proper word highlighting.

user_journeys.title: Navigating via transcript click-to-seek
user_journeys.description: A user uses the transcript panel to quickly jump between different parts of the clip.

steps.action: User sees a list of utterances in the transcript panel
steps.system_behavior: TranscriptPanel renders all utterances with word-level spans. Each word has word-level timing data.
steps.user_sees: Transcript text with the active utterance highlighted. Words are clickable.

steps.action: User clicks the word 'hurricane' in an utterance near the start
steps.system_behavior: onClick handler reads word.startSec from the utterance's words array. Calls seekTo(word.startSec - clipStartSec). Video seeks to that absolute time.
steps.user_sees: Video jumps to the moment 'hurricane' is spoken. Timeline playhead jumps. Caption overlay shows the word group around 'hurricane' with it highlighted.

steps.action: User clicks a word in a different utterance further down
steps.system_behavior: Same flow: seekTo with the word's timestamp.
steps.user_sees: Video jumps to that moment. Transcript auto-scrolls to show the new active utterance.

user_journeys.title: Changing caption position and style
user_journeys.description: A user repositions captions from bottom to top and adjusts the outline.

steps.action: User opens the Captions panel from the tool sidebar
steps.system_behavior: setActiveTool('captions'). CaptionsPanel renders with current preset values.
steps.user_sees: Caption styling controls. Position shows 'Bottom' as active.

steps.action: User clicks 'Top' position button
steps.system_behavior: setCaptionPreset updates position to 'top'. CaptionOverlay re-renders with top: '10%' positioning.
steps.user_sees: Caption overlay jumps from bottom of video to top of video, 10% from the top edge.

steps.action: User increases outline width from 2 to 4 using the slider
steps.system_behavior: setCaptionPreset updates outlineWidth to 4. CaptionOverlay regenerates text-shadow with wider outline.
steps.user_sees: Caption text gets a thicker black outline, making it more readable against bright backgrounds.

steps.action: User changes outline color from black to dark red (#8B0000)
steps.system_behavior: setCaptionPreset updates outlineColor. CaptionOverlay regenerates text-shadow with new color.
steps.user_sees: Caption outline changes from black to dark red.

steps.action: User clicks 'Center' position button
steps.system_behavior: setCaptionPreset updates position to 'center'. CaptionOverlay re-renders with top: '50%' + transform: 'translateY(-50%)'.
steps.user_sees: Caption overlay moves to vertically centered on the video.

user_journeys.title: Export/render after editing
user_journeys.description: After editing transcript and styling captions, user triggers a render and downloads the result.

steps.action: User has finished editing transcript and styling captions. They click the Export button.
steps.system_behavior: Export dropdown shows options (or triggers render). API call: POST /api/projects/{id}/clips/render with { clipIds: [clipId], aspectRatios: ['9:16'] }.
steps.user_sees: Export button/dropdown. Render starts.

steps.action: Worker picks up the render job
steps.system_behavior: Worker fetches clip with updated transcriptSlice (containing edited text + word timing) and captionPreset. generateSrtFromSlice() creates SRT with 2-3 word cues from words[]. FFmpeg burns captions with preset styling.
steps.user_sees: Progress indicator shows rendering status.

steps.action: Render completes
steps.system_behavior: ClipRender status = 'completed'. Rendered MP4 uploaded to R2.
steps.user_sees: Render complete notification. Download/preview available.

steps.action: User downloads and reviews the rendered clip
steps.system_behavior: GET /api/projects/{id}/clips/{clipId}/download returns presigned URL.
steps.user_sees: Downloaded video has: edited transcript text as captions, rapid 2-3 word cue changes, correct font/color/position/outline from captionPreset. The content matches what they previewed in the studio editor.

user_journeys.title: Fallback experience for clips without word timing
user_journeys.description: A clip that was transcribed before the word-timing update still works in the editor.

steps.action: User opens a clip whose transcriptSlice has utterances WITHOUT words[] array
steps.system_behavior: page.tsx loads data normally. utterances have text, startSec, endSec but no words field.
steps.user_sees: Studio loads normally with video and transcript.

steps.action: User plays the video
steps.system_behavior: useCurrentCaption finds active utterance. words is undefined/empty. Falls back to splitting utterance.text by whitespace. Returns all words with isActive: false.
steps.user_sees: Captions show the full utterance text (not a sliding window). No per-word highlighting (all words same color). Still readable and functional.

steps.action: User edits the transcript text
steps.system_behavior: updateUtteranceText recalculates with proportional redistribution. New words[] are created with proper timing.
steps.user_sees: After editing, the caption overlay now has word-level timing and per-word highlighting works for the edited utterance.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Caption overlay must update at minimum 10fps (every 100ms) during playback without visible lag or jank
non_functional_requirements.implementation: useCurrentCaption uses useMemo with currentTime dependency. The video timeupdate event fires roughly every 250ms by default. For smoother updates, consider requestAnimationFrame polling when isPlaying.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Video seeking (clicking timeline, arrow keys, word click) must respond within 200ms
non_functional_requirements.implementation: video.currentTime setter triggers immediate seek. R2 supports range requests for fast random access.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Auto-save must not lose data. If two saves are in-flight, the second waits for the first.
non_functional_requirements.implementation: Debounce with cleanup — clearTimeout on new changes cancels pending save. Only one save in-flight at a time.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: All schema changes must be backward-compatible. Existing data must pass validation without modification.
non_functional_requirements.implementation: All new fields are z.optional(). TranscriptUtterance.words is optional. CaptionPreset new fields are optional.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Source video presigned URLs must expire after 1 hour and only be generated for authenticated users with project access.
non_functional_requirements.implementation: requireCurrentAppUser() in server component. presignDownloadUrl with expiresIn: 3600. URL is per-session, not cached.

non_functional_requirements.requirement: Keyboard shortcuts must work as documented. Editing mode must not capture keyboard shortcuts.
non_functional_requirements.implementation: Existing keyboard handler (lines 242-310 in studio-shell.tsx) already checks if target is INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT. contentEditable elements should also be excluded.

technical_constraints.reason: transcriptSlice and captionPreset are both Json/JSONB columns. Zod schemas validate at runtime. New fields are optional.

technical_constraints.constraint: Worker rendering cannot replicate all browser preview effects
technical_constraints.reason: FFmpeg ASS subtitles have limited styling compared to CSS. highlightColor (per-word color switching) and animation (bounce, karaoke) are preview-only. This is acceptable and matches industry standard.

technical_constraints.constraint: Video must be accessible via presigned R2 URL with CORS headers
technical_constraints.reason: Browser <video> element needs to load cross-origin content. R2 bucket must have appropriate CORS configuration.

technical_constraints.constraint: Auto-save debounce must not trigger on initial page load
technical_constraints.reason: useRef guard prevents the auto-save effect from firing when the component mounts with initial prop values.

out_of_scope: Caption animation modes beyond word-by-word (karaoke, bounce)
ASS file generation for word-level color in rendered output
Video trimming/cropping UI (resize handles are present but non-functional)
Undo/redo for transcript edits (only segment operations have undo/redo currently)
